name: Cerebellar cortex: layers and circuit
summary: The cerebellar cortex is a uniform three-layered sheet folded into thousands of folia: an outer molecular layer of parallel fibers, stellate and basket cells; a single row of Purkinje cells; and an inner granular layer packed with granule cells and Golgi cells. Two afferent systems enter it. Mossy fibers from the pontine nuclei, spinal cord and vestibular nuclei excite granule cells, whose axons rise to the molecular layer and split into parallel fibers that run along the folium and excite the flat dendritic trees of thousands of Purkinje cells. Climbing fibers from the contralateral inferior olive each wrap around a single Purkinje cell and fire a complex spike that teaches it. Purkinje cells are the only output, inhibiting the deep nuclei. The uniformity of this circuit is why the cerebellum applies the same computation to movement, gaze and cognition, and its cell types are the targets of specific diseases: Purkinje cells in alcohol, paraneoplastic and hypoxic injury, granule cells in medulloblastoma.

anatomy.location: The gray matter covering the folia of the whole cerebellum, about 1 mm thick, with the same three layers everywhere; the Purkinje layer separates the outer molecular layer from the inner granular layer, and the white matter core carries the afferent and efferent fibers to the deep nuclei.

subdivisions.name: Molecular layer
subdivisions.note: parallel fibers, Purkinje dendrites, stellate and basket cells

subdivisions.name: Purkinje cell layer
subdivisions.note: single row of large GABAergic output neurons

subdivisions.name: Granular layer
subdivisions.note: granule cells (the most numerous neurons in the brain), Golgi cells, mossy fiber glomeruli

afferents.from: Pontine nuclei, spinal cord, vestibular nuclei, reticular formation
afferents.via: mossy fibers via all three peduncles
climbing fibers via the inferior cerebellar peduncle

efferents.via: direct Purkinje projection from the flocculonodular lobe and vermis

function: Mossy fiber input is expanded by the granule cells into a sparse code carried by the parallel fibers, which Purkinje cells read through about 200,000 synapses each; climbing fiber input signals errors and induces long-term depression at the parallel fiber synapses that were active just before, so that the Purkinje cell learns to predict and correct the error, the basis of motor learning and of the adaptation of the vestibulo-ocular reflex. Basket and stellate cells sharpen the Purkinje output in space and Golgi cells in time. Purkinje cells inhibit the deep nuclei and the vestibular nuclei, sculpting the excitatory signal that collaterals of the mossy and climbing fibers have already delivered there, so that the cerebellum's output is a timed modulation rather than a command.

bestView.label: cerebellar cortex and white matter arbor vitae

imaging.normalAppearance: The cortex forms the gray rim of each folium with the white matter arbor vitae branching into it; the layers are below MRI resolution but the folial pattern is sharp on T1 and the cortex is slightly brighter than white matter on FLAIR. Cerebellar atrophy widens the fissures and thins the folia.

pathology.finding: Widened cerebellar fissures with thin folia, diffuse in spinocerebellar ataxias, paraneoplastic degeneration and phenytoin toxicity, anterior vermian in alcohol.
Restricted diffusion outlining the folia (gyriform) in the border zones or in the whole cortex after cardiac arrest, reflecting Purkinje cell vulnerability.
Cellular tumor of granule cell lineage in the vermis and fourth ventricle with restricted diffusion and enhancement.
Striated 'tiger-stripe' thickening of the folia of one hemisphere (dysplastic gangliocytoma) in Cowden syndrome.

lesionEffects.mechanism: Loss of Purkinje cell timing of the deep nuclear output
Diffuse Purkinje cell loss in toxic, paraneoplastic and hereditary degenerations

lesionEffects.deficit: Impaired motor learning and VOR adaptation

lesionEffects.mechanism: Posterior lobe cortical involvement disturbing the cerebro-cerebellar cognitive loops

examination: Standard cerebellar examination: finger-nose, heel-shin, rapid alternating movements, tandem gait
Eye movements: gaze-evoked and downbeat nystagmus, saccadic pursuit
Cognitive screening in diffuse cerebellar disease
pearls: Purkinje cells are among the most vulnerable neurons in the brain: alcohol, hypoxia, hyperthermia, phenytoin and anti-Yo antibodies kill them selectively
Every part of the cerebellar cortex has the same circuit; what differs is where the input comes from and where the output goes
Anti-Yo paraneoplastic degeneration in a woman with ovarian or breast cancer produces a subacute pancerebellar syndrome with a normal MRI at first

pitfalls: Cerebellar cortical atrophy on MRI in the elderly may be asymptomatic; correlate with the examination
